_comment: Every value here is available in ALL templates as {{ site.xxx }}.
This is the Eleventy equivalent of PHP config constants.
For example, {{ site.name }} outputs your site name in any .njk file.
When reusing this boilerplate for a new project, update these
values and the entire site adapts automatically.
_comment_identity: Change these first on a new site. url has NO trailing slash — templates append page paths ("https://example.com" + "/about/").
name: My Site
description: A short description of your site
_comment_locale: Same idea, two formats — so both live here:
lang   = BCP 47 tag with a hyphen (en, nb, nb-NO) → <html lang>, JSON-LD inLanguage, manifest lang, humans.txt.
locale = Open Graph's language_TERRITORY with an UNDERSCORE (en_US, nb_NO) → og:locale. A page can override it with `locale:` front matter.
_comment_alternateName: Other names Google may show as the site name in search results (an acronym, short form or the domain), e.g. ["D-FAULT", "dfault.it"]. Goes in the home page's WebSite JSON-LD only. [] = none.
_comment_version: Footer version. Bump with `npm run bump:patch|minor|major`. (On Daniel's machine, a global Claude Code Stop hook reminds you if src/ changes go uncommitted without a bump.)
_comment_author: Who BUILT the website — Daniel on every site, also when the site is ABOUT someone else (credit the subject in the page content, not here).
Used by <meta name="author">, humans.txt, llms.txt and the JSON-LD Person node on every page.
id = one stable URI for the same person on EVERY site (JSON-LD @id), so search engines can see that all the sites share one author.
sameAs = other pages that are unmistakably the same person (Daniel's site network).
_comment_publisher: Who OWNS the site → JSON-LD WebSite.publisher (home page) and the mainEntity of a `schemaType: ProfilePage` page.
Leave id empty (Daniel's own sites): the author above is also the publisher — no extra node.
Client/company site: type "Organization", its own id (e.g. https://client.no/#organization), name, url, logo (square PNG/JPG ≥112x112 px, root-relative or full URL) and its profiles in sameAs.
type "Person" uses image (a portrait) instead — logo is only valid on an Organization.
_comment_security: expires: "" = build date + 1 year, recomputed on every build (src/_data/build.js). Set a fixed ISO date (e.g. "2027-05-06T00:00:00.000Z") instead if you want the file to go stale as a reminder to re-check the contact — RFC 9116 recommends less than a year ahead.
_comment_robots: robots = default <meta name="robots"> for every page; a page overrides it with its own `robots:` front matter.
"index, follow" alone is Google's default and does nothing; max-image-preview:large allows big image previews (Search, Discover).
A page whose robots contains "noindex" (e.g. robots: "noindex, follow") is ALSO left out of sitemap.xml and llms.txt.

noindexSite = true for a staging/private site: every page gets noindex, nofollow (meta tag + X-Robots-Tag header from .htaccess) and sitemap.xml/llms.txt are emptied/switched off — but robots.txt keeps crawling ALLOWED, because a blocked crawler never sees the noindex.
_comment_ai: AI crawler policy → src/robots.njk (bot names: src/_data/aiBots.js). true = allowed. Default: everything allowed (be found, cited AND trained on).

train:     GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended, Meta-ExternalAgent, CCBot. NOTE Google-Extended also controls Gemini-app grounding, so false also drops the site from Gemini answers (Google Search and AI Overviews are unaffected).
search:    OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Meta-WebIndexer. false = not cited in those assistants' search answers.

userFetch: ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, Perplexity-User, Meta-ExternalFetcher (a person asked an assistant to open a page). OpenAI, Perplexity and Meta say these may ignore robots.txt, so false is a request, not a block.
contentSignal: also print Cloudflare's Content-Signal line (search/ai-input/ai-train = yes|no) — a stated preference nobody is obliged to honour.

Never blocked here: Googlebot, Bingbot, Applebot, facebookexternalhit — they feed Google/Bing/Siri (incl. AI Overviews and Copilot) and link previews. Opting out of Google AI Overviews/AI Mode is a Search Console setting, not robots.txt.
_comment_llms: llmsTxt = publish /llms.txt (https://llmstxt.org): a Markdown map of the site for AI tools, built from the pages (noindex pages, `llms: false` pages and demo pages left out). No big AI provider officially reads it and Google ignores it — it's cheap, so it's on. false = not built.
_comment_seo: Share image + browser colour → head-meta.njk (Open Graph, X card, JSON-LD) and site.webmanifest.njk.

themeColor tints Chrome's address bar on Android (and an installed app's title bar). Match the navbar: the boilerplate navbar is bg-primary = #0d6efd in plain Bootstrap 5.3 — change both together if you pick a Bootswatch theme or another navbar colour.

ogImage: landscape 1200x630, under ~300 KB (WhatsApp skips bigger ones), not just a logo. Facebook/Telegram cache share images by URL, so head-meta.njk adds ?v=<hash of the file's content> (the `v` filter in eleventy.config.js): a new picture under the same name gets a new URL by itself. (.htaccess lets browsers keep images for a month.)
ogImageAlt describes the PICTURE, not the page. Width/height/type must match the real file. A page with its own ogImage can set ogImageAlt/ogImageWidth/ogImageHeight/ogImageType in front matter.
ogImageAlt: dfault — Eleventy + Bootstrap 5 Boilerplate: glowing neon logo next to stacked translucent layers
_comment_social: Optional, "" = tag left out. x = X/Twitter handle WITHOUT @ → twitter:site. fediverse = Mastodon handle like @user@instance → fediverse:creator (Mastodon only shows the byline if that account lists this domain under Edit profile → Verification → Author attribution).
_comment_analytics: Google Analytics measurement ID. Leave empty string to disable.
_comment_gaConsent: How GA waits for the visitor — only matters when gaId is set. Your call per site:
"implied" = GA loads on the first page view and the cookie toast only informs (the boilerplate's behaviour so far).

"required" = opt-in: GA loads only after Accept in the cookie toast (Accept / Decline, no X). Decline or no answer = GA never loads; Decline after an earlier Accept switches GA off and deletes its _ga cookies. In this mode the legal page's Cookie Policy shows a 'Change my cookie choice' button (data-dd-cookie-settings, re-opens the toast) so visitors can change their answer; add the same attribute to any other button that should do that.
For Norwegian/EU visitors, "required" is the safe choice: Norway's revised ekomloven (2025) is read as asking for GDPR-standard consent to analytics cookies — check Datatilsynet's current guidance.
_comment_bootswatch: Default Bootswatch theme loaded on first visit (all visitors). 'default' = plain Bootstrap. Theme names, CDN URLs and SRI hashes live in src/_data/cdn.js.
_comment_flat: flatToggle: the Flat mode button in the offcanvas menu (square corners, no shadows — flat.css) plus its JS in bundle.js. false = the button is gone AND a visitor's saved Flat choice is ignored, so nobody is stuck in flat mode with no way out. A site.json without the key counts as true.
_comment_devtools: DEV/DEMO TOOLS — handy while building, rarely wanted on a finished site. The boilerplate shows them; on a derived site set BOTH to false before launch:
bootswatchSwitcher: the Bootswatch theme picker in the offcanvas menu (plus its JS in bundle.js).

demoPages: the demo pages (today /cheatsheet/, the Bootstrap component page) and their nav.js entries (`demo: true`). false = the pages aren't built at all. Either way they're noindex and never in sitemap.xml or llms.txt.
_comment_fonts: Google Fonts URL. Leave empty string to keep the theme's own fonts (system fonts for plain Bootstrap; most Bootswatch themes load Google Fonts themselves, see noGoogleFonts in src/_data/cdn.js). Example: 'https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;700&display=swap'
_comment_fontOverride: true = adds .dd-font-override to <html>, so the --bs-font-sans-serif stack in style.css §1.0 wins over Bootstrap's / the Bootswatch theme's own font. Set it together with googleFontsUrl, and put your font first in that stack. A site.json without the key counts as false.
_comment_navbar: The navbar's background utility (bg) and its own data-bs-theme (theme) → navbar.njk. Default bg-primary + dark = white text on the primary colour.

With a light-primary Bootswatch theme (minty, brite) white text fails contrast: use { "bg": "bg-body-tertiary", "theme": "light" } or { "bg": "bg-dark", "theme": "dark" }. Change themeColor above to match. A site.json without the key gets the default.
_comment_webmanifest: PWA manifest → site.webmanifest.njk. name/shortName: "" = use site.name (shortName is the label under the home-screen icon, keep it ≤12 characters). theme_color comes from site.themeColor above (add webmanifest.themeColor only to override it). backgroundColor = splash-screen colour while an installed app starts.
_comment_footer: Footer configuration. 'links' renders as paired rows on mobile (centered bi-slash separator) and as one inline line on desktop.
Any number of links works: footer.njk pairs them with batch(2) and centres an odd last one on mobile. A link to this site's own domain (www. ignored) shows as plain text instead of linking to itself.
